html:
From the late 1600s men from Bermuda sailed each season to Grand Turk and Salt Cay to rake salt from the shallow ponds. Salt was the islands' main trade for close to three hundred years.

The Bermudians dug ponds, built sluices and brought enslaved Africans to do the hard work. The salt went to the North American colonies, above all to preserve the fish of New England and Newfoundland.

Spain, France and the Bahamas all disputed the islands at times. The trade faded in the 20th century and ended in the 1960s. The old ponds and the town of Cockburn Town on Grand Turk still show it.
